svg.aria-label: Kafka-style distributed log. A topic is split into partitions; producers choose the partition by hashing the key, so one key's messages stay in order. Each partition is an append-only log of segment files on disk, with a leader on one broker and followers on others; a write is acknowledged once the in-sync replicas have it. Consumers in a group each own some partitions and commit the offset they have processed, so they can resume after a crash and other groups can read the same data independently. A controller, using Raft, assigns partition leaders and handles broker failures. Old segments are deleted by time or size, or compacted to keep the latest value per key.
